title: Finiteness and discreteness of a complementary pure-subcurve boundary
statement: Let X be a reduced Noetherian Jacobson scheme and i:Y→X a reduced closed subscheme. Suppose every irreducible component of X and Y has topological Krull dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let j be the inclusion of the scheme-theoretic image of the open complement of i. The scheme pullback T=Y×_X image(j) [def-pc-fibre-product] has a finite discrete underlying space, and its image points in X are closed. Empty subcurves and empty intersections are allowed.

proof.text: Use the reduced-image theorem to identify the complementary image with the reduced closure of the open complement. Apply the complementary-component-union theorem to get complementary subsets I,J of the finite irreducible-component set.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: For different components C,D, C minus D is nonempty and open in the irreducible one-dimensional component C. Its complement is finite. The boundary is contained in the finite union of these finite intersections.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: The boundary image is closed and finite. In a Jacobson space its points are closed: closed points are dense in every closed subset, and a finite subspace can have no nonclosed point when its closed points are dense in all its closed subsets. The boundary immersion is injective, so its source is finite and T1, hence discrete.

lean.statement:
theorem complementary_pure_subcurve_boundary_finite
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [IsNoetherian X] [JacobsonSpace X]
    (hX : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, topologicalKrullDim C = 1)
    (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsReduced Y]
    (hY : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Y, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) :
    let j := (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι
    Finite (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i j) ∧ DiscreteTopology (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i j) ∧
      ∀ t : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i j, IsClosed ({i (pullback.fst i j t)} : Set X)
